targets.name: GitHub OAuth app: server-side authorization code + S256 PKCE with client secret, REST API /user
notes: GitHub publishes no discovery document (https://github.com/.well-known/openid-configuration answered 404 on 2026-09-27); the endpoints below are trusted explicit metadata from GitHub's documentation, which states S256 is the only PKCE method
GET https://api.github.com/user without credentials answered 401 with no WWW-Authenticate header (2026-09-27); the Bearer provider answers challenge-less 401s from its configured resources
the client secret is sent as a form parameter (client_secret_post), as the documentation's examples do

unattended (session mode): plausible but unverified — an already-authorized OAuth app with unchanged scopes is redirected without a consent click, but GitHub may demand device verification, 2FA or re-authentication for a stored session; any such page makes the non-interactive login fail closed

env.name: RA_INTEROP_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET

env.name: RA_INTEROP_GITHUB_USER_ID
env.description: numeric id of the test GitHub account (the /user response's id) to assert the identity (required: strict results must be tied to the configured test account)

env.name: RA_INTEROP_GITHUB_REDIRECT_URI
env.description: loopback redirect URI registered for the test client (default http://127.0.0.1:39398/callback)

env.name: RA_INTEROP_GITHUB_STORAGE_STATE
env.description: Playwright storageState file of a dedicated test account's signed-in identity-provider session (contains cookies; never commit). With --headed it seeds the browser; without --headed it enables the fail-closed non-interactive session mode (a configured file that does not exist is a configuration error)

capabilityNotes.refreshRotation: GitHub documents single-use refresh tokens for GitHub Apps; the OAuth-app page documents refresh tokens with offline_access but not their rotation: to be observed

capabilityNotes.audienceRestriction: the negative-audience scenario needs the harness's local introspecting API (see keycloak-no-audience); this target calls the provider's own API

targets.name: Google OAuth 2.0 web-server flow without GIS: confidential client, access_type=offline + consent, OpenID userinfo
notes: discovery 2026-09-27: issuer https://accounts.google.com, revocation_endpoint https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke, PKCE plain and S256
GET https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo without credentials answered 401 with no WWW-Authenticate header (2026-09-27)
Google returns a refresh token for access_type=offline only on consent (hence prompt=consent) and does not return a new one on refresh
Google's OpenID documentation allows ID tokens with iss accounts.google.com (without https://); the library requires the discovered issuer exactly, so such a token would FAIL rather than be accepted

unattended (session mode): not expected to work — this target sends prompt=consent (Google returns a refresh token only on consent), so every authorization shows a consent page, and Google may block automated browsers; run it headed

targets.name: Microsoft Entra ID v2.0 authorization code + S256 PKCE without MSAL, Microsoft Graph /me
notes: discovery of a tenant-specific v2.0 issuer (2026-09-27): issuer https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant-id}/v2.0, no revocation_endpoint, token auth client_secret_post/client_secret_basic
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me without credentials answered 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer (2026-09-27)
use the tenant ID (GUID): 'common' and domain names discover an issuer that differs from the configured one
the Web platform accepts http redirect URIs only on localhost (the portal refuses http://127.0.0.1), hence the localhost default; SPA redirect URIs cannot be redeemed server-side
Microsoft documents that each refresh returns a new refresh token while the old one is not revoked

unattended (session mode): only in a test tenant where the test user has no MFA/Conditional Access prompt and consent is already granted; security defaults require MFA periodically, which fails closed; unverified
